student_facing_description: Evaluates how you used open-ended questions, affirmations, reflective listening, and summaries to guide a patient-centered conversation.
what_it_evaluates: Use of OARS motivational-interviewing micro-skills: Open-ended questions that invite the patient's own words; Affirmations that recognize patient strengths and efforts; Reflections that demonstrate active listening by restating or deepening what the patient said; Summaries that consolidate information before transitions.
criteria: Open-ended questions are used to open topics and explore patient perspectives rather than defaulting to yes/no questions.
Closed questions are reserved for clarification, not for opening new topics.
The student reflects patient statements (simple or complex reflections) rather than only acknowledging with 'okay' or 'I see'.
Affirmations are genuine and specific to something the patient said or did.
The student summarizes key information at transitions or before closing.
Questions build on the patient's previous answers instead of following a fixed checklist order.
Leading or suggestive questions that plant an answer are avoided.
